description: Per-release compatibility and migration guidance for the Charter specification, schemas, conformance corpus, and Go reference SDK. Newest first. README.md documents the current state; this file is the versioned history GOVERNANCE.md requires of every release.

field_notes.version: semantic version of the repository release and Go module tag (v<version>); the body identifies the supported specification and schema versions

migrations.title: Principal-aware Keel permission gate
migrations.summary: Corrects the optional Keel adapter's permission interface for keel v1.2.62 and passes principal-aware grant subjects through `PermissionGate`. Agent actors can now be authorized directly against a keel `agent` grant source instead of requiring a synthetic user mapping. The Charter specification, schema catalogue, and conformance profiles are unchanged from 1.0.0.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Versions

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`, `x-charter-schema-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.0.2 |
| Optional keel adapter (`sdk/adapter/keel`) | keel v1.2.62 |

## Compatibility impact

The normative Charter contract and all document formats remain compatible with 1.0.0. Version 1.0.1 updated the token identity type but left Charter's local `PermissionChecker` on keel's old user-id signature. That interface compiled in isolation, but `port.DatabaseRepository` no longer satisfied it. Version 1.0.2 corrects the adapter contract:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `PermissionChecker.CheckActionPermission(ctx, userID int, ...)` | `PermissionChecker.CheckActionPermission(ctx, principal model.Principal, ...)` |
| `IdentityMap.UserID(ctx, actor)` | `IdentityMap.Principal(ctx, actor)` |

`PermissionGate` now passes the grant-evaluation `model.Principal` to `CheckActionPermission`, and a compile-time assertion verifies that `port.DatabaseRepository` satisfies `PermissionChecker`.

`BaseClaimIdentityMap` maps a human actor to `model.UserPrincipal` using its `keel_user_id` claim. It maps an agent actor directly to `model.Principal{Kind: "agent", ID: actor.ID}`; an agent token no longer needs a `keel_user_id` claim. Register the corresponding `agent` grant source in keel before repository initialization. If that source declares extra filters, provide a custom `IdentityMap` that returns their values in `Principal.Scope` in registration order. Charter's authority model remains platform-neutral and unchanged.

## Adoption

1. Upgrade with `go get github.com/nauticana/charter@v1.0.2`.
2. Update custom `PermissionChecker` implementations to accept `model.Principal`, and replace custom `IdentityMap.UserID` methods with `Principal`.
3. For human actors, return `model.UserPrincipal(userID)`. For agent actors, register a keel `agent` grant source and return its principal kind, stable id, and any configured scope values.
4. Wire `PermissionGate.Keel` directly to a keel v1.2.62 `port.DatabaseRepository` implementation and run the downstream test suite. No Charter documents, schemas, fixtures, or conformance claims require migration.

migrations.title: Keel 1.2.62 compatibility
migrations.summary: Updates the optional Keel adapter from keel v1.2.61 to v1.2.62 and adopts Keel's renamed OAuth token identity type. The Charter specification, schema catalogue, conformance profiles, and runtime behavior are unchanged from 1.0.0.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Versions

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`, `x-charter-schema-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.0.1 |
| Optional keel adapter (`sdk/adapter/keel`) | keel v1.2.62 |

## Compatibility impact

The normative Charter contract and all document formats remain compatible with 1.0.0. The optional Go adapter has one source-level migration caused by keel v1.2.62 moving OAuth token identity out of its interface-only `port` package:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `*port.Principal` | `*model.TokenPrincipal` |
| `Session.Principal *port.Principal` | `Session.Principal *model.TokenPrincipal` |
| `JobContext(ctx, *port.Principal, ...)` | `JobContext(ctx, *model.TokenPrincipal, ...)` |

This token identity is distinct from keel's new `model.Principal`, which represents the subject of a database grant decision. Charter's authority model remains platform-neutral and is unchanged.

## Adoption

1. Upgrade with `go get github.com/nauticana/charter@v1.0.1`.
2. If using `sdk/adapter/keel`, upgrade keel to v1.2.62.
3. Replace constructed or referenced `port.Principal` values with `model.TokenPrincipal`; update imports from `github.com/nauticana/keel/port` to `github.com/nauticana/keel/model` where the token principal was the only port symbol used.
4. Run the downstream test suite. No Charter documents, schemas, fixtures, or conformance claims require migration.

migrations.title: First release
migrations.summary: First released version of the Charter specification (12 chapters, 111 requirements), the 40-kind schema catalogue with three conformance format schemas, the conformance corpus (core-model: 20 semantic rules; agent-runtime: 8 and system-adapter: 4 runtime-behavioral rules; 45 fixtures), the Go reference SDK, the charter CLI, and the optional keel adapter.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Versions

| Artifact | Version |
|---|---|
| Specification (`charterSpecVersion`, `x-charter-spec-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Schema catalogue (`catalogVersion`, `x-charter-schema-version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Conformance manifest (`specification.version`) | 1.0.0 |
| Go module `github.com/nauticana/charter` | v1.0.0 |
| Optional keel adapter (`sdk/adapter/keel`) | keel v1.2.55 |

## Compatibility impact

None: this is the first release. Documents written against the unreleased `draft` version must set `charterSpecVersion` to `1.0.0`; `charter validate` rejects any other value. Action records must carry the `disposition` introduced with CHR-EVID-010.

## Conformance

All 45 manifest fixtures pass; the reference SDK's claims for the three active profiles are committed under `conformance/claims/` and regenerated by `charter claim` on every release. Per CHR-CONF-010, later minor and patch releases keep these fixtures runnable.

## Adoption

1. `go get github.com/nauticana/charter@v1.0.0`.
2. Validate documents with `charter validate -conformance conformance <dir>`.
3. Runtimes implement `validate.Subject`, adapters `validate.AdapterSubject`, and claim a profile with `charter claim`.
